title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is §5 of Grothendieck's notes on stratified spaces: germs of conic and cylindrical neighbourhoods and the 'déploiement' (unfolding). The previous page defined germs of conic neighbourhoods T of Y ⊂ X, meaning T up to the homotheties λT. It then observed that if Ẋ ⊂ X̃* carries a germ of cylindrical neighbourhoods and Ẋ → Y is continuous, the pushout X = X̃* ⊔_Ẋ Y inherits a germ of conic neighbourhoods of Y.

Main statement. Grothendieck compares two categories.
(a) Systems (X̃*, Ẋ, ℰ, Y, f), where:
- X̃* is a topological space;
- Ẋ is a closed subset of X̃*;
- ℰ is a germ of cylindrical (collar-type) neighbourhoods Ẋ×[0,ε) of Ẋ in X̃*;
- Y is a topological space;
- f : Ẋ → Y is an arbitrary continuous map.
(b) Triples (X, Y, τ), where Y is closed in X and τ is a germ of conic neighbourhoods of Y in X.

The obvious functor (a)→(b) sends a system to X = X̃* ⊔_Ẋ Y. Near Y this space is the mapping cylinder of f, so it carries a germ of conic neighbourhoods; the radial coordinate is the collar coordinate. Grothendieck asserts that this functor is an equivalence of categories.

The inverse is the 'unfolding'. Choose a representative conic neighbourhood T with link Ṫ and retraction Ṫ → Y. Cut out the open cone λT minus λṪ and keep the boundary λṪ. Equivalently, X̃* = X* ⊔ Ẋ with X* = X∖Y, the deleted cone being replaced by its 'base' Ẋ ≅ Ṫ, and f is the link projection. Working with germs makes this independent of λ.

This is the depth-one case of the dévissage of a stratified space into a 'manifold with boundary + boundary map to the singular stratum'. It is done here for bare topological spaces, with no fibration condition on f. The previous page notes that the conic structure is 'restrictive' exactly when f is fibrant.

Margin notes.
- There is a variant with 'tubes' instead of germs, which also gives an equivalence of categories, apparently for a restricted class of morphisms (reading uncertain).
- (X̃*, Ẋ) with its cylindrical germ is described as a 'découpe' (cutting) of X along (Y, τ).

Subsets. A subset X' ⊂ X corresponds to a pair of subsets X̃'* ⊂ X̃*, Y' ⊂ Y with the same inverse image in Ẋ. X' is closed iff both are. X' is compatible with the conic germ τ iff X̃' is compatible with the cylindrical germ ℰ. One should then normalize X̃' to X̃'_1 = closure of X'∩X*, where X* = X̃∖Ẋ; its germ near Ẋ is determined by X̃'_1∩Ẋ.

The next page turns this into a corollary: compatible closed subsets correspond 1-1 to pairs (X̃', Y') with X̃' cylinder-compatible and f(Ẋ') ⊂ Y'. Such an X' is strictly conic iff Y' = f(Ẋ'). The next page then starts the treatment of transversality between cylindrical and conic germs, the step needed to iterate the construction over several strata.
errors: The categories' morphisms are not specified. With (b)-morphisms taken as all continuous maps X→X' sending Y to Y' and compatible with the conic germs, the functor is not full/essentially an equivalence: a map can send points of X∖T into Y', and then it does not lift to X̃*→X̃'*. One needs stratum-preserving morphisms, i.e. φ^{-1}(Y') = Y, together with compatibility with radial coordinates and homotheties on germs. Faithfulness is fine, since Ẋ lies in the closure of X* thanks to the collar.

The notation drifts between X̃* and X̃ (and X̃' vs X̃'*). Grothendieck himself corrects by introducing X* = X̃∖Ẋ and X̃'_1 = closure(X'∩X*). The 'same inverse image in Ẋ' condition for arbitrary subsets is correct, but compatibility requires the normalization X̃'_1, as he notes.

No fibration or properness hypothesis on f is needed for the equivalence as stated at the purely topological level; this is consistent. The previous page links fibrancy of f only to the 'restrictive' property.

ideas.what: Equivalence of categories between (space with closed subspace and germ of conic neighbourhood) and (space with collared closed 'boundary' Ẋ plus arbitrary continuous map f: Ẋ→Y), via the mapping-cylinder pushout X = X̃* ⊔_Ẋ Y and its inverse 'cutting/unfolding'
ideas.modern_name: Unfolding / resolution / 'unzip' of a depth-one stratified space (blow-up along a stratum to a manifold with boundary with a fibered boundary map); mapping cylinder neighbourhoods
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather control data (1969–70); Verona (unfolding of abstract stratified spaces, 1984); Brasselet–Hector–Saralegi (unfoldings, 1990s); Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (resolution to manifolds with fibered corners, 2012); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzip, 2017); Quinn (homotopy links/mapping cylinder neighbourhoods, 1988)
ideas.where_published: Only programmatically: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6, announces a 'dévissage' theorem identifying tame stratified spaces with systems of 'manifolds with boundary/corners' and gluing maps. The precise depth-one topological statement is not published.

ideas.what: Germs of cylindrical/conic neighbourhoods (equivalence up to homothety λT) used so that the cutting construction is canonical
ideas.modern_name: Germs of tubular/collar neighbourhoods; control data up to shrinking
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather; Siebenmann (1972) for topological stratified sets

ideas.what: Correspondence between compatible closed subsets X' of X and pairs (X̃', Y') with X̃' cylinder-compatible, f(Ẋ') ⊂ Y' (strict iff equality)
ideas.modern_name: Substratifications/closed unions of strata described via their unfoldings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in the resolution literature (Verona; Albin et al.)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, at the level of bare topological spaces and with no fibration hypothesis on the attaching map, the depth-one 'déploiement' as an explicit equivalence of categories between conic-germ data (X, Y, τ) and cut data (X̃*, Ẋ, ℰ, Y, f). It is a precursor of the Ayala–Francis–Tanaka 'unzip' and of the Albin–Mazzeo et al. resolution, which work in smooth or conically smooth settings. The idea is announced in the Esquisse, but this precise categorical form (and the subset dictionary) is not in print.
missed.quote: Alors le foncteur ci-dessus évident de a) dans b) est une équivalence de catégories. Rappelons que X = X̃* ⊔_Ẋ Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a purely topological, germ-based version of the unzip equivalence. It isolates fibrancy of the link map as a separate, optional condition ('restrictif ssi fibrant'), which matches the homotopically stratified (Quinn) versus Thom–Mather distinction. However, the content is close to known results, and the morphisms must be restricted for the claim to be true.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, explicit categorical form of the depth-one unfolding, previously known from Grothendieck only programmatically via the Esquisse, now in a general topological setting. But the mathematics is essentially the standard mapping-cylinder/resolution picture, later developed independently (Verona, Quinn, Albin et al., Ayala–Francis–Tanaka), and the page leaves morphisms unspecified.
transcription_corrections: Opening line: 'Considérons les deux catégories' ('deux' inserted above the line), with a) and b) labelling the two categories; 'couples' crossed out and replaced by 'systèmes'.
Margin NB at bottom left reads roughly: 'NB (X̃*, Ẋ), germe de voisinage cylindrique de Ẋ: une "découpe" cônique le long de (Y, τ)'. The word is likely 'découpe' (cutting) of X along (Y, τ).

Top-left diagonal margin note reads roughly: 'NB Il y a une variante avec des "tubes" au lieu de germes de voisinages cylindriques (resp. côniques), aussi! équivalence de catégories, pour les morphismes ...'. The final qualifier on the morphisms is uncertain.
'il faut et suffit qu'il en soit ainsi de X̃'' is a likelier reading than 'qu'il en soit de'.

Last lines: 'Il y a lieu alors de remplacer X̃' par X̃'_1 = closure(X'∩X*) (où X* = X̃∖Ẋ), et le germe de X̃'_1 au voisinage de Ẋ ...' — 'au voisinage' rather than 'voisinage [?]'; the sentence continues on the next page.
